name_en: Ikanago no kugini — sand lance simmered in soy sauce, sugar, and ginger until glossy
summary_ja: 春先にとれる稚魚のイカナゴを、醤油と砂糖、生姜だけでつやが出るまで煮詰めた瀬戸内の甘辛い佃煮。仕上がりが曲がった錆びくぎに似ることからこの名がついたと伝わり、炊きあがる香りに春を感じる家庭も多いという。
summary_en: A Seto Inland Sea preserve made by simmering baby sand lance in soy sauce, sugar, and ginger until dark and glossy. The curled shapes are said to resemble bent, rusted nails, and the smell of it cooking is said to mark the start of spring for many households.
source_publisher: 農林水産省「うちの郷土料理」

name_en: Katsumeshi — beef cutlet over rice with demi-glace sauce and cabbage
summary_ja: 薄めに盛ったご飯に平たいビーフカツをのせ、デミグラスソースをかけてゆでキャベツを添えた加古川の洋食。箸で気軽に食べられるようにと戦後の食堂で考案されたと伝わり、店ごとにたれや具材の違いを楽しめる。
summary_en: A Kakogawa yoshoku dish of thin-pounded beef cutlet over a shallow bed of rice, topped with demi-glace sauce and boiled cabbage. It is said to have been devised at a postwar diner so it could be eaten easily with chopsticks, and each restaurant now has its own take on the sauce.
source_publisher: 農林水産省「うちの郷土料理」

name_en: Yude matsuba-gani — snow crab boiled whole in seawater-strength brine
summary_ja: 山陰で松葉ガニと呼ばれるズワイガニを、海水よりやや薄い塩水でまるごと茹でる但馬地域の冬の味覚。冷めても身にほんのりとした甘みが残るとされ、二杯酢につけて食べるほか雑炊やコロッケにも使われる。
summary_en: Snow crab, called matsuba-gani on the Sea of Japan coast, boiled whole in brine slightly weaker than seawater — a winter taste of the Tajima region. The meat is said to keep a faint sweetness even once cooled, and is dipped in vinegar-soy or worked into rice porridge and croquettes.
source_publisher: 農林水産省「うちの郷土料理」

name_en: Sansho no tsukudani — Japanese pepper berries simmered down in soy and mirin
summary_ja: 養父市朝倉の朝倉山椒や神戸市有馬の有馬山椒を、醤油とみりんで汁気がなくなるまで煮詰めた佃煮。とげのない木になる朝倉山椒は献上品にもされたと伝わり、炊きたてのご飯や冷や奴の薬味として食べられている。
summary_en: Japanese pepper berries from Yabu's Asakura district or Kobe's Arima area, simmered down in soy sauce and mirin until the liquid is gone. Asakura sansho, grown on a thornless tree, is said to have once been presented to the shogunate, and the finished preserve is eaten over hot rice or as a garnish for chilled tofu.
source_publisher: 農林水産省「うちの郷土料理」

name_ja: 高野豆腐粉と野菜の煮物
name_en: Koya-dofu-ko to yasai no nimono — freeze-dried tofu powder simmered with root vegetables
summary_ja: 高野豆腐を作る過程で出る粉を、鶏肉やニンジン、ゴボウ、干しシイタケと一緒にだし汁で煮て仕上げる多可町の家庭料理。町内に一軒残る製造業者から手に入る「とふ粉」を使い、家庭の味として受け継がれている。
summary_en: A Taka Town home dish made by simmering chicken, carrot, burdock, and dried shiitake in dashi, then stirring in the powder left over from making freeze-dried tofu. The powder still comes from the town's one remaining maker, and the dish is passed down as a family recipe.
source_title: 高野豆腐粉と野菜の煮物
source_publisher: 農林水産省「うちの郷土料理」

name_en: Kuromame ni — Tanba black soybeans simmered sweet for New Year
summary_ja: 丹波篠山特産の丹波黒大豆を、醤油と砂糖でしわが寄らないようじっくり甘く煮た正月料理。皮が破れにくく大粒で糖度が高いとされ、近年はポリフェノールが注目され通年食べる家庭も増えているという。
summary_en: Tanba-Sasayama's prized black soybeans, simmered slowly and sweetly in soy sauce and sugar with care taken to keep the skins from wrinkling — a New Year dish. The beans are said to be large, sweet, and slow to split, and more households are said to now eat it year-round for its polyphenols.
source_publisher: 農林水産省「うちの郷土料理」

name_en: Jabu — chicken and vegetables simmered without added water
summary_ja: 鶏肉と豆腐、糸こんにゃく、季節の野菜を水を使わずに醤油とみりんで煮る新温泉町の料理。具材から出る水分で汁がじゃぶじゃぶと音を立てることが名前の由来とされ、祭りや冠婚葬祭で大鍋にして振る舞われてきた。
summary_en: A Shin'onsen Town dish of chicken, tofu, shirataki noodles, and seasonal vegetables simmered in soy sauce and mirin without any added water. The name is said to come from the sloshing sound the vegetables' own juices make as they cook, and it has long been made in a big pot to share at festivals and family gatherings.
source_publisher: 農林水産省「うちの郷土料理」
